points.t: A **painless, slowly enlarging swollen foot** with **multiple discharging sinuses** in someone from an endemic tropical area.
Soil **fungi (eumycetoma)** or **actinomycete bacteria (actinomycetoma)** implanted by a thorn or wound form **grains** in deep tissue.
Specialist diagnosis (grain culture, deep biopsy, imaging); long antibiotics for actinomycetoma; antifungals + surgery for eumycetoma.
**Bone involvement** and late presentation → amputation; other causes of sinuses (TB, osteomyelitis, HS).

cause.lead: Soil organisms that build colonies under the skin.
points: **Triad**: painless firm swelling + multiple sinuses + **discharge with grains**.
**Eumycetoma** (fungal, e.g. *Madurella mycetomatis*) vs **actinomycetoma** (*Nocardia*, *Actinomadura*, *Streptomyces*).
‘Mycetoma belt’ ~15°S–30°N: **Sudan**, West Africa, Yemen, India, Mexico, Venezuela, Brazil; UK cases in migrants.
Thorn / splinter inoculation in barefoot rural workers; no person-to-person spread; incubation months–years.
Actinomycetoma invades bone earlier; **black grains = fungal**.

features.lead: Slow, painless, sinuses that heal and reopen.
points: ~**70% foot**; also hand, leg, knee; back / shoulder / head in load carriers.
Small painless nodule (‘boil’ or ‘cyst’) → swelling → nodules soften and **open as sinuses**.
Serous / purulent discharge **with grains**; sinuses heal and new ones open; skin hyperpigmented, shiny.
Pain mild until bone or secondary infection; **systemically well**.
Late: massive swelling, deformity, bone destruction.

visuals.caption: Mycetoma: a swollen forefoot with multiple sinus openings discharging fluid containing tiny grains; shake the gauze in saline to see them (black grains suggest a fungal cause).
visuals.alt: Swollen foot with discharging sinuses and inset of black grains on gauze

points: Shake discharge gauze in saline; dermoscopy.
**Deep surgical biopsy / FNA** (not swabs): microscopy, stains, slow culture (tell the lab), histology, PCR.
X-ray (periosteal reaction, lytic bone), ultrasound, **MRI ‘dot-in-circle’**, CT.

cards.name: Chronic osteomyelitis
cards.clue: Sinus over bone, prior fracture, metalwork, diabetic foot; no grains.

cards.name: Scrofuloderma / NTM
cards.clue: Over nodes or bone; AFB; undermined sinuses.

cards.name: Podoconiosis / lymphoedema
cards.clue: Mossy foot, no sinuses with grains.

manage.lead: Primary care: recognise, avoid repeated antibiotics or incision, refer.

points: Every suspected case → **ID / tropical medicine** (e.g. HTD) with orthopaedics / plastics and dermatology.
**Urgent** if spreading toward trunk or scalp, rapid progression or sepsis.
Treat acute secondary infection per NICE cellulitis guidance; clean dressings; analgesia; elevation; **tetanus check**; footwear advice.
**Actinomycetoma**: usually medically curable with prolonged combination antibiotics.
**Eumycetoma**: long antifungals (e.g. itraconazole) + surgery.
**Itraconazole**: capsules need food and acid (avoid PPIs / antacids); strong CYP3A4 inhibitor (simvastatin, some DOACs, CCBs, colchicine…); LFTs; avoid in heart failure.
**Co-trimoxazole** for months: FBC, potassium, renal function, rash; avoid with methotrexate; warfarin / phenytoin interactions.

limits.t: Incise, partially excise, or label as ‘recurrent cellulitis / abscess’.

items.t: Bone pain, deformity, rapid spread: urgent specialist imaging and referral.
Any suspected mycetoma: ID / tropical medicine.

pearls.t: Farmer whose foot keeps ‘discharging’ despite antibiotics → mycetoma, osteomyelitis or TB. Ask where they grew up and whether barefoot.
Painless is a warning sign, not a comfort.

quiz.a: Painless swelling, multiple sinuses, discharge with grains.

quiz.q: Which form is usually medically curable?
Why not incise in primary care?
quiz.a: Inadequate excision causes recurrence and spread.
